div.head: Prologus
div.p: Not out of envy, for there’s no effect Where there’s no cause; nor out of imitation, For we have ever more been imitated; Nor out of our contention to do better Than that which is opposed to ours in title, For that was good, and better cannot be. And for the title, if it seem affected We might as well have called it, ‘God you good even’, Only that eastward westwards still exceeds – Honour the sun’s fair rising, not his setting. Nor is our title utterly enforced, As by the points we touch at you shall see. Bear with our willing pains, if dull or witty; We only dedicate it to the city.

div2.stage: Enter Master TOUCHSTONE and QUICKSILVER at several doors, QUICKSILVER with his hat, pumps, short sword, and dagger, and a [tennis] racket trussed up under his cloak. At the middle door, enter GOLDING discovering a goldsmith’s shop and walking short turns before it.

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: [To Quicksilver] And whither with you now? What loose action are you bound for? Come, what comrades are you to meet withal? Where’s the supper? Where’s the rendezvous?

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Indeed, and in very good sober truth, sir –

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: ‘Indeed, and in very good sober truth, sir’! Behind my back thou wilt swear faster than a French footboy and talk more bawdily than a common midwife, and now ‘indeed, and in very good sober truth, sir’! But if a privy search should be made, with what furniture are you rigged now? Sirrah, I tell thee I am thy master, William Touchstone, goldsmith, and thou my prentice, Francis Quicksilver, and I will see whither you are running. Work upon that now!

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Why, sir, I hope a man may use his recreation with his master’s profit.

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: Prentices’ recreations are seldom with their masters’ profit. Work upon that now! You shall give up your cloak, though you be no alderman. (Touchstone uncloaks Quicksilver.) Heyday, Ruffians’ Hall! Sword, pumps, here’s a racket indeed.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Work upon that now!

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: Thou shameless varlet, dost thou jest at thy lawful master contrary to thy indentures?

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Why, ’sblood, sir, my mother’s a gentlewoman and my father a Justice of Peace and of Quorum, and though I am a younger brother and a prentice, yet I hope I am my father’s son; and by God’s lid, ’tis for your worship and for your commodity that I keep company. I am entertained among gallants, true. They call me cousin Frank, right. I lend them moneys, good. They spend it, well. But when they are spent, must not they strive to get more? Must not their land fly? And to whom? Shall not Your Worship ha’ the refusal? Well, I am a good member of the city if I were well considered. How would merchants thrive, if gentlemen would not be unthrifts? How could gentlemen be unthrifts if their humours were not fed? How should their humours be fed but by white meat and cunning secondings? Well, the city might consider us. I am going to an ordinary now: the gallants fall to play; I carry light gold with me; the gallants call, ‘Cousin Frank, some gold for silver!’; I change, gain by it; the gallants lose the gold and then call ‘Cousin Frank, lend me some silver.’ Why –

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: Why? I cannot tell. Seven score pound art thou out in the cash, but look to it, I will not be gallanted out of my moneys. And as for my rising by other men’s fall, God shield me! Did I gain my wealth by ordinaries? No. By exchanging of gold? No. By keeping of gallants company? No. I hired me a little shop, fought low, took small gain, kept no debt book, garnished my shop, for want of plate, with good wholesome thrifty sentences, as ‘Touchstone, keep thy shop and thy shop will keep thee’; ‘Light gains makes heavy purses’; ‘’Tis good to be merry and wise.’ And when I was wived, having something to stick to, I had the horn of suretyship ever before my eyes. You all know the device of the horn, where the young fellow slips in at the butt end and comes squeezed out at the buccal. And I grew up, and, I praise Providence, I bear my brows now as high as the best of my neighbours. But thou – well, look to the accounts; your father’s bond lies for you; seven score pound is yet in the rear.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Why, ’slid, sir, I have as good, as proper, gallants’ words for it as any are in London, gentlemen of good phrase, perfect language, passingly behaved, gallants that wear socks and clean linen and call me ‘kind cousin Frank’, ‘good cousin Frank’, for they know my father. And by God’s lid, shall not I trust ’em? Not trust?

div2.stage: Enter a PAGE as inquiring for TOUCHSTONE’S shop.

sp.speaker: GOLDING
sp.p: What do ye lack, sir? What is’t you’ll buy, sir?

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: Ay, marry, sir, there’s a youth of another piece. There’s thy fellow prentice, as good a gentleman born as thou art, nay, and better meaned. But does he pump it or racket it? Well, if he thrive not, if he outlast not a hundred such crackling bavins as thou art, God and men neglect industry.

sp.speaker: GOLDING
sp.p: (To the Page) It is his shop, and here my master walks.

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: With me, boy?

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: My master, Sir Petronel Flash, recommends his love to you and will instantly visit you.

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: To make up the match with my eldest daughter, my wife’s dilling, whom she longs to call madam. He shall find me unwillingly ready, boy. Exit Page. There’s another affliction, too. As I have two prentices, the one of a boundless prodigality, the other of a most hopeful industry, so have I only two daughters, the eldest of a proud ambition and nice wantonness, the other of a modest humility and comely soberness. The one must be ladified, forsooth, and be attired just to the court cut and long tail. So far is she ill-natured to the place and means of my preferment and fortune that she throws all the contempt and despite hatred itself can cast upon it. Well, a piece of land she has, ’twas her grandmother’s gift: let her, and her Sir Petronel, flash out that. But as for my substance, she that scorns me as I am a citizen and tradesman shall never pamper her pride with my industry, shall never use me as men do foxes: keep themselves warm in the skin and throw the body that bare it to the dunghill. I must go entertain this Sir Petronel. [To Golding] Golding, my utmost care’s for thee, and only trust in thee. Look to the shop. [To Quicksilver] As for you, Master Quicksilver, think of husks, for thy course is running directly to the prodigal’s hogs’ trough. Husks, sirrah! Work upon that now.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Marry faugh, goodman flat cap! ’Sfoot, though I am a prentice I can give arms, and my father’s a justice o’ peace by descent, and ’sblood –

sp.speaker: GOLDING
sp.p: Fie, how you swear!

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: ’Sfoot, man, I am a gentleman, and may swear by my pedigree, God’s my life. Sirrah Golding, wilt be ruled by a fool? Turn good fellow, turn swaggering gallant, and ‘let the welkin roar, and Erebus also’. Look not westward to the fall of Don Phoebus, but to the east – eastward ho!

lg.l: ‘Where radiant beams of lusty Sol appear,
And bright Eoüs makes the welkin clear.’

sp.p: We are both gentlemen, and therefore should be no coxcombs. Let’s be no longer fools to this flat cap Touchstone. Eastward, bully! This satin-belly and canvas-backed Touchstone – ’slife, man, his father was a maltman and his mother sold gingerbread in Christ Church.

sp.speaker: GOLDING
sp.p: What would ye ha’ me do?

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Why, do nothing; be like a gentleman, be idle. The curse of man is labour. Wipe thy bum with testons and make ducks and drakes with shillings. What, eastward ho! Wilt thou cry, ‘What is’t ye lack?’, stand with a bare pate and a dropping nose under a wooden penthouse, and art a gentleman? Wilt thou bear tankards and mayst bear arms? Be ruled, turn gallant, eastward ho! [He sings.] ‘Ta lirra, lirra, ro.’ [He declaims.] ‘Who calls Jeronimo? Speak, here I am.’ God’s so, how like a sheep thou look’st! O’my conscience, some cowherd begot thee. Thou Golding of Golding Hall, ha, boy?

sp.speaker: GOLDING
sp.p: Go, ye are a prodigal coxcomb. I a cowherd’s son because I turn not a drunken whore-hunting rakehell like thyself?

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Rakehell? Rakehell?

div2.stage: [Quicksilver] offers to draw, and Golding trips up his heels and holds him.

sp.speaker: GOLDING
sp.p: Pish! In soft terms ye are a cowardly bragging boy. I’ll ha’ you whipped.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Whipped? That’s good, i’faith. Untruss me?

sp.speaker: GOLDING
sp.p: No, thou wilt undo thyself. Alas, I behold thee with pity, not with anger. Thou common shot-clog, gull of all companies, methinks I see thee already walking in Moorfields without a cloak, with half a hat, without a band, a doublet with three buttons, without a girdle, a hose with one point and no garter, with a cudgel under thine arm, borrowing and begging threepence.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Nay, ’slife, take this and take all. As I am a gentleman born, I’ll be drunk, grow valiant, and beat thee.

sp.speaker: GOLDING
sp.p: Go, thou most madly vain, whom nothing can recover but that which reclaims atheists and makes great persons sometimes religious: calamity. As for my place and life, thus I have read:

lg.l: ‘Whate’er some vainer youth may term disgrace,
The gain of honest pains is never base.
From trades, from arts, from valour honour springs;
These three are founts of gentry, yea, of kings.’

div2.stage: Enter GERTRUDE, MILDRED, BETTRICE, and POLDAVY a tailor, Poldavy with a fair gown, Scotch farthingale, and French fall in his arms; Gertrude in a French head attire and citizen’s gown; Mildred sewing; and Bettrice leading a monkey after her.

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: For the passion of patience, look if Sir Petronel approach, that sweet, that fine, that delicate, that – for love’s sake tell me if he come. Oh, sister Mil, though my father be a low-capped tradesman, yet I must be a lady, and, I praise God, my mother must call me medam. Does he come? Off with this gown, for shame’s sake, off with this gown! Let not my knight take me in the city cut in any hand. Tear’t, pax on’t! Does he come? Tear’t off.

lg.l: [Sings.] ‘Thus whilst she sleeps I sorrow for her sake,’ etc.

sp.speaker: MILDRED
sp.p: Lord, sister, with what an immodest impatiency and disgraceful scorn do you put off your city tire! I am sorry to think you imagine to right yourself in wronging that which hath made both you and us.

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: I tell you I cannot endure it. I must be a lady. Do you wear your coif with a London licket, your stammel petticoat with two guards, the buffin gown with the tuftaffety cape and the velvet lace. I must be a lady, and I will be a lady. I like some humours of the city dames well: to eat cherries only at an angel a pound, good; to dye rich scarlet black, pretty; to line a grogram gown clean through with velvet, tolerable. Their pure linen, their smocks of three pound a smock are to be borne withal. But your mincing niceries, taffeta pipkins, durance petticoats, and silver bodkins – God’s my life, as I shall be a lady I cannot endure it. Is he come yet? Lord, what a long knight ’tis!

lg.l: [Sings.] ‘And ever she cried, “Shoot home!”’–

sp.p: and yet I knew one longer –

lg.l: ‘and ever she cried, “Shoot home!”
Fa, la, ly, re, lo, la.’

sp.speaker: MILDRED
sp.p: Well, sister, those that scorn their nest oft fly with a sick wing.

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: Bow-bell!

sp.speaker: MILDRED
sp.p: Where titles presume to thrust before fit means to second them, wealth and respect often grow sullen and will not follow. For sure, in this I would for your sake I spake not truth. ‘Where ambition of place goes before fitness of birth, contempt and disgrace follow.’ I heard a scholar once say that Ulysses, when he counterfeited himself mad, yoked cats and foxes and dogs together to draw his plough, whilst he followed and sowed salt. But sure I judge them truly mad that yoke citizens and courtiers, tradesmen and soldiers, a goldsmith’s daughter and a knight. Well, sister, pray God my father sow not salt too.

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: Alas, poor Mil! When I am a lady I’ll pray for thee yet, i’faith. Nay, and I’ll vouchsafe to call thee sister Mil still, for though thou art not like to be a lady as I am, yet sure thou art a creature of God’s making, and mayst peradventure to be saved as soon as I. – Does he come? –

lg.l: [Sings.] ‘And ever and anon she doubled in her song.’

sp.p: Now lady’s my comfort, what a profane ape’s here! Tailor, Poldavis, prithee fit it, fit it! Is this a right Scot? Does it clip close and bear up round?

sp.speaker: POLDAVY
sp.p: Fine and stiffly, i’faith. ’Twill keep your thighs so cool and make your waist so small! Here was a fault in your body, but I have supplied the defect with the effect of my steel instrument, which, though it have but one eye, can see to rectify the imperfection of the proportion.

div2.stage: [He puts the farthingale and new gown on her.]

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: Most edifying tailor! I protest, you tailors are most sanctified members and make many crooked things go upright. How must I bear my hands? Light? Light?

sp.speaker: POLDAVY
sp.p: Oh, ay, now you are in the lady fashion you must do all things light. Tread light, light. Ay, and fall so; that’s the court amble.

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: Has the court ne’er a trot?

sp.speaker: POLDAVY
sp.p: No, but a false gallop, lady.

lg.l: (She sings.) ‘And if she will not go to bed –’.

sp.speaker: BETTRICE
sp.p: The knight’s come, forsooth.

div2.stage: Enter Sir PETRONEL, Master TOUCHSTONE, and MISTRESS TOUCHSTONE [and GOLDING].

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: Is my knight come? Oh, the lord, my band! Sister, do my cheeks look well? Give me a little box o’the ear that I may seem to blush. Now, now! So, there, there, there! Here he is. O my dearest delight! Lord, lord, and how does my knight?

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: Fie, with more modesty!

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: Modesty! Why, I am no citizen now. Modesty! Am I not to be married? You’re best to keep me modest now I am to be a lady.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: Boldness is good fashion, and court-like.

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: Ay, in a country lady I hope it is, as I shall be. And how chance ye came no sooner, knight?

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: Faith, I was so entertained in the progress with one Count Epernoum, a Welsh knight. We had a match at balloon, too, with my Lord Whachum, for four crowns.

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: At baboon? Jesu! You and I will play at baboon in the country, knight.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: Oh, sweet lady, ’tis a strong play with the arm.

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: With arm, or leg, or any other member, if it be a court sport. And when shall ’s be married, my knight?

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: I come now to consummate it, an your father may call a poor knight son-in-law.

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: Sir, ye are come. What is not mine to keep I must not be sorry to forego. A hundred pound land her grandmother left her, ’tis yours. Herself (as her mother’s gift) is yours. But if you expect aught from me, know, my hand and mine eyes open together; I do not give blindly. Work upon that now.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: Sir, you mistrust not my means? I am a knight.

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: Sir, sir, what I know not, you will give me leave to say I am ignorant of.

sp.speaker: MRS TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: Yes, that he is a knight! I know where he had money to pay the gentlemen ushers and heralds their fees. Ay, that he is a knight, and so might you have been, too, if you had been aught else than an ass, as well as some of your neighbours. An I thought you would not ha’ been knighted, as I am an honest woman I would ha’ dubbed you myself. I praise God I have wherewithal. But as for you, daughter –

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: Ay, mother. I must be a lady tomorrow, and by your leave, mother – I speak it not without my duty, but only in the right of my husband – I must take place of you, mother.

sp.speaker: MRS TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: That you shall, lady-daughter, and have a coach as well as I, too.

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: Yes, mother. But by your leave, mother – I speak it not without my duty, but only in my husband’s right – my coach horses must take the wall of your coach horses.

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: Come, come, the day grows low, ’tis supper time. Use my house; the wedding solemnity is at my wife’s cost. Thank me for nothing but my willing blessing, for – I cannot feign – my hopes are faint. And sir, respect my daughter; she has refused for you wealthy and honest matches, known good men, well monied, better traded, best reputed.

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: Body o’truth, chitizens, chitizens! Sweet knight, as soon as ever we are married, take me to thy mercy out of this miserable chitty; presently carry me out of the scent of Newcastle coal and the hearing of Bow-bell. I beseech thee, down with me, for God’s sake!

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: Well, daughter, I have read that old wit sings:

lg.l: ‘The greatest rivers flow from little springs.
Though thou art full, scorn not thy means at first;
He that’s most drunk may soonest be athirst.’

sp.p: Work upon that now! (All but Touchstone, Mildred, and Golding depart.) No, no; yond stand my hopes. – Mildred, come hither, daughter. And how approve you your sister’s fashion? How do you fancy her choice? What dost thou think?

sp.speaker: MILDRED
sp.p: I hope, as a sister, well.

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: Nay, but, nay, but, how dost thou like her behaviour and humour? Speak freely.

sp.speaker: MILDRED
sp.p: I am loath to speak ill, and yet – I am sorry of this – I cannot speak well.

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: Well, very good. As I would wish, a modest answer. – Golding, come hither; hither, Golding. [Golding comes forward.] How dost thou like the knight, Sir Flash? Does he not look big? How lik’st thou the elephant? He says he has a castle in the country.

sp.speaker: GOLDING
sp.p: Pray heaven the elephant carry not his castle on his back.

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: ’Fore heaven, very well! But seriously, how dost repute him?

sp.speaker: GOLDING
sp.p: The best I can say of him is, I know him not.

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: Ha, Golding! I commend thee, I approve thee, and will make it appear my affection is strong to thee. My wife has her humour, and I will ha’ mine. Dost thou see my daughter here? She is not fair, well-favoured, or so – indifferent – which modest measure of beauty shall not make it thy only work to watch her, nor sufficient mischance to suspect her. Thou art towardly, she is modest; thou art provident, she is careful. She’s now mine. Give me thy hand; she’s now thine. Work upon that now!

sp.speaker: GOLDING
sp.p: Sir, as your son I honour you, and as your servant obey you.

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: Sayest thou so? – Come hither, Mildred. Do you see yond fellow? He is a gentleman, though my prentice, and has somewhat to take to; a youth of good hope, well friended, well parted. Are you mine? You are his. Work you upon that now!

sp.speaker: MILDRED
sp.p: Sir, I am all yours. Your body gave me life, your care and love happiness of life. Let your virtue still direct it, for to your wisdom I wholly dispose myself.

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: Say’st thou so? Be you two better acquainted. Lip her, lip her, knave! [Golding kisses Mildred.] So, shut up shop; in. We must make holiday.

lg.l: This match shall on, for I intend to prove
Which thrives the best, the mean or lofty love;
Whether fit wedlock vowed ’twixt like and like,
Or prouder hopes, which daringly o’erstrike
Their place and means. ’Tis honest time’s expense
When seeming lightness bears a moral sense.
Work upon that now!

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: Quicksilver! Master Francis Quicksilver! Master Quicksilver!

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Here, sir. (Ump!)

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: So, sir. Nothing but flat Master Quicksilver, without any familiar addition, will fetch you. Will you truss my points, sir?

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Ay, forsooth. (Ump!)

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: How now, sir? The drunken hiccup so soon this morning?

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: ’Tis but the coldness of my stomach, forsooth.

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: What? Have you the cause natural for it? You’re a very learned drunkard; I believe I shall miss some of my silver spoons with your learning. The nuptial night will not moisten your throat sufficiently, but the morning likewise must rain her dews into your gluttonous weasand.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: An’t please you, sir, we did but drink (ump!) to the coming off of the knightly bridegroom.

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: To the coming off o’him?

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Ay, forsooth. We drunk to his coming on (ump!) when we went to bed, and now we are up we must drink to his coming off. For that’s the chief honour of a soldier, sir, and therefore we must drink so much the more to it, forsooth. (Ump!)

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: A very capital reason. So that you go to bed late and rise early to commit drunkenness? You fulfil the scripture very sufficient wickedly, forsooth.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: The knight’s men, forsooth, be still o’their knees at it, (ump!) and because ’tis for your credit, sir, I would be loath to flinch.

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: I pray, sir, e’en to ’em again then. You’re one of the separated crew, one of my wife’s faction, and my young lady’s, with whom and with their great match I will have nothing to do.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: So, sir. Now I will go keep my (ump!) credit with ’em, an’t please you, sir.

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: In any case, sir, lay one cup of sack more o’your cold stomach, I beseech you.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Yes, forsooth.

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: This is for my credit! Servants ever maintain drunkenness in their master’s house ‘for their master’s credit’; a good idle servingman’s reason. I thank Time the night is past; I ne’er waked to such cost. I think we have stowed more sorts of flesh in our bellies than ever Noah’s ark received. And for wine, why, my house turns giddy with it, and more noise in it than at a conduit. Ay me, even beasts condemn our gluttony. Well, ’tis our city’s fault, which, because we commit seldom, we commit the more sinfully. We lose no time in our sensuality, but we make amends for it. Oh, that we would do so in virtue and religious negligences! (Enter GOLDING and MILDRED, [opening the shop and] sitting on either side of the stall.) But see, here are all the sober parcels my house can show. I’ll eavesdrop, hear what thoughts they utter this morning.

sp.speaker: GOLDING
sp.p: [To Mildred] But is it possible that you, seeing your sister preferred to the bed of a knight, should contain your affections in the arms of a prentice?

sp.speaker: MILDRED
sp.p: I had rather make up the garment of my affections in some of the same piece than like a fool wear gowns of two colours or mix sackcloth with satin.

sp.speaker: GOLDING
sp.p: And do the costly garments – the title and fame of a lady, the fashion, observation, and reverence proper to such preferment – no more inflame you than such convenience as my poor means and industry can offer to your virtues?

sp.speaker: MILDRED
sp.p: I have observed that the bridle given to those violent flatteries of fortune is seldom recovered. They bear one headlong in desire from one novelty to another, and where those ranging appetites reign, there is ever more passion than reason; no stay, and so no happiness. These hasty advancements are not natural. Nature hath given us legs to go to our objects, not wings to fly to them.

sp.speaker: GOLDING
sp.p: How dear an object you are to my desires I cannot express, whose fruition, would my master’s absolute consent and yours vouchsafe me, I should be absolutely happy. And though it were a grace so far beyond my merit that I should blush with unworthiness to receive it, yet thus far both my love and my means shall assure your requital: you shall want nothing fit for your birth and education; what increase of wealth and advancement the honest and orderly industry and skill of our trade will afford in any, I doubt not will be aspired by me; I will ever make your contentment the end of my endeavours; I will love you above all; and only your grief shall be my misery, and your delight, my felicity.

p.seg: Work upon that now! By my hopes, he woos honestly and orderly; he shall be anchor of my hopes. Look, see the ill-yoked monster, his fellow.

div2.stage: Enter QUICKSILVER unlaced, a towel about his neck, in his flat cap, drunk.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Eastward ho! ‘Holla, ye pampered jades of Asia!’

p.seg: Drunk now downright, o’my fidelity!

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: (Ump!) Pulldo, pulldo! ‘Showse’, quoth the caliver.

sp.speaker: GOLDING
sp.p: Fie, fellow Quicksilver, what a pickle are you in?

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Pickle? Pickle in thy throat! Zounds, pickle? Wa ha ho! Good morrow, Knight Petronel; ’morrow, lady goldsmith. Come off, knight, with a counterbuff, for the honour of knighthood.

sp.speaker: GOLDING
sp.p: Why, how now, sir? Do ye know where you are?

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Where I am? Why, ’sblood, you jolthead, where I am?

sp.speaker: GOLDING
sp.p: Go to, go to! For shame, go to bed and sleep out this immodesty; thou sham’st both my master and his house.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Shame? What shame? I thought thou wouldst show thy bringing up. An thou wert a gentleman as I am, thou wouldst think it no shame to be drunk. Lend me some money, save my credit; I must dine with the servingmen and their wives – and their wives, sirrah!

sp.speaker: GOLDING
sp.p: E’en who you will. I’ll not lend thee threepence.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: ’Sfoot, lend me some money. ‘Hast thou not Hiren here?’

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: [Coming forward] Why, how now, sirrah? What vein’s this, hah?

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: ‘Who cries on murder? Lady, was it you?’ How does our master? Pray thee, cry, ‘Eastward ho!’

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: Sirrah, sirrah, you’re past your hiccup now; I see you’re drunk.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: ’Tis for your credit, master.

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: And hear you keep a whore in town.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: ’Tis for your credit, master.

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: And what you are out in cash, I know.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: So do I. My father’s a gentleman; work upon that now! Eastward ho!

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: Sir, ‘Eastward, ho!’ will make you go ‘Westward, ho!’ I will no longer dishonest my house nor endanger my stock with your licence. There, sir, there’s your indenture. [He hands him a document.] All your apparel – that I must know – is on your back, and from this time my door is shut to you. From me be free, but for other freedom and the moneys you have wasted, ‘Eastward ho!’ shall not serve you.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Am I free o’my fetters? Rent, fly with a duck in thy mouth! And now I tell thee, Touchstone –

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: Good sir.

lg.l: ‘When this eternal substance of my soul’ –

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: Well said. Change your gold ends for your play ends.

lg.l: ‘Did live imprisoned in my wanton flesh’ –

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: What then, sir?

lg.l: ‘I was a courtier in the Spanish court,
And Don Andrea was my name.’

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: Good master Don Andrea, will you march?

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Sweet Touchstone, will you lend me two shillings?

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: Not a penny.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Not a penny? I have friends, and I have acquaintance. I will piss at thy shop posts and throw rotten eggs at thy sign. Work upon that now!

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: [To Golding] Now, sirrah, you! Hear you! You shall serve me no more neither, not an hour longer.

sp.speaker: GOLDING
sp.p: What mean you, sir?

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: I mean to give thee thy freedom, and with thy freedom my daughter, and with my daughter a father’s love. And with all these such a portion as shall make Knight Petronel himself envy thee. You’re both agreed, are ye not?

sp.speaker: BOTH [GOLDING and MILDRED]
sp.p: [Kneeling] With all submission, both of thanks and duty.

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: [Raising them] Well, then, the great power of heaven bless and confirm you! And, Golding, that my love to thee may not show less than my wife’s love to my eldest daughter, thy marriage feast shall equal the knight’s and hers.

sp.speaker: GOLDING
sp.p: Let me beseech you, no, sir. The superfluity and cold meat left at their nuptials will with bounty furnish ours. The grossest prodigality is superfluous cost of the belly. Nor would I wish any invitement of states or friends; only your reverend presence and witness shall sufficiently grace and confirm us.

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: Son to mine own bosom, take her and my blessing! The nice fondling, my lady sir-reverence, that I must not now presume to call daughter, is so ravished with desire to hansel her new coach and see her knight’s eastward castle that the next morning will sweat with her busy setting forth. Away will she and her mother, and while their preparation is making, ourselves, with some two or three other friends, will consummate the humble match we have in God’s name concluded.

l.emph: ’Tis to my wish, for I have often read
‘Fit birth, fit age, keeps long a quiet bed.’
’Tis to my wish, for tradesmen, well ’tis known,
Get with more ease than gentry keeps his own.

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: My privy guest, lusty Quicksilver, has drunk too deep of the bridebowl, but with a little sleep he is much recovered and I think is making himself ready to be drunk in a gallanter likeness. My house is, as ’twere, the cave where the young outlaw hoards the stolen vails of his occupation; and here, when he will revel it in his prodigal similitude, he retires to his trunks and – I may say softly – his punks. He dares trust me with the keeping of both, for I am security itself; my name is Security, the famous usurer.

div2.stage: Enter QUICKSILVER in his prentice’s coat and cap [and] his gallant breeches and stockings, gartering himself. SECURITY [meets him].

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Come, old Security, thou father of destruction. Th’indented sheepskin is burned wherein I was wrapped, and I am now loose to get more children of perdition into thy usurous bonds. Thou feed’st my lechery, and I thy covetousness; thou art pandar to me for my wench, and I to thee for thy cozenages. ‘Ka me, ka thee’, runs through court and country.

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: Well said, my subtle Quicksilver. These K’s ope the doors to all this world’s felicity; the dullest forehead sees it. Let not master courtier think he carries all the knavery on his shoulders. I have known poor Hob in the country, that has worn hobnails on’s shoes, have as much villainy in’s head as he that wears gold buttons in’s cap.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Why, man, ’tis the London highway to thrift; if virtue be used, ’tis but as a scrap to the net of villainy. They that use it simply, thrive simply, I warrant. Weight and fashion makes goldsmiths cuckolds.

div2.stage: Enter SINDEFY, with Quicksilver’s doublet, cloak, rapier, and dagger.

sp.speaker: SINDEFY
sp.p: Here, sir, put off the other half of your prenticeship.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER

lg.l: Well said, sweet Sin! Bring forth my bravery.
Now let my trunks shoot forth their silks concealed.
I now am free and now will justify
My trunks and punks. Avaunt, dull flat cap, then!
Via, the curtain that shadowed Borgia!
lg.stage: [He tosses away his prentice’s hat and coat.]
lg.l: There lie, thou husk of my envassalled state.
I, Samson now, have burst the Philistines’ bands
And in thy lap, my lovely Delilah,
I’ll lie and snore out my enfranchised state.
lg.stage: [He attires himself as a gallant, with rapier and dagger.]
lg.l: [Sing.] ‘When Samson was a tall young man
His power and strength increasèd then.’
He sold no more, nor cup, nor can,
But did them all despise.
Old Touchstone, now write to thy friends
For one to sell thy base gold ends;
Quicksilver now no more attends
Thee, Touchstone.

sp.p: [To Security] But Dad, hast thou seen my running gelding dressed today?

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: That I have, Frank. The ostler o’the Cock dressed him for a breakfast.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: What, did he eat him?

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: No, but he eat his breakfast for dressing him, and so dressed him for breakfast.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Oh, witty age, where age is young in wit, And all youth’s words have greybeards full of it!

sp.speaker: SINDEFY
sp.p: But, alas, Frank, how will all this be maintained now? Your place maintained it before.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Why, and I maintained my place. I’ll to the court – another manner of place for maintenance, I hope, than the silly city. I heard my father say, I heard my mother sing, an old song and a true: ‘Thou art a she fool, and know’st not what belongs to our male wisdom.’ I shall be a merchant, forsooth! Trust my estate in a wooden trough as he does? What are these ships but tennis balls for the winds to play withal? Tossed from one wave to another, now under line, now over the house; sometimes brick-walled against a rock, so that the guts fly out again; sometimes struck under the wide hazard, and farewell Master Merchant.

sp.speaker: SINDEFY
sp.p: Well, Frank, well, the seas, you say, are uncertain. But he that sails in your court seas shall find ’em ten times fuller of hazard, wherein to see what is to be seen is torment more than a free spirit can endure. But when you come to suffer, how many injuries swallow you? What care and devotion must you use to humour an imperious lord? Proportion your looks to his looks, smiles to his smiles? Fit your sails to the wind of his breath?

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Tush, he’s no journeyman in his craft that cannot do that.

sp.speaker: SINDEFY
sp.p: But he’s worse than a prentice that does it, not only humouring the lord, but every trencher-bearer, every groom, that by indulgence and intelligence crept into his favour and by pandarism into his chamber. He rules the roost, and when my honourable lord says, ‘It shall be thus’, my worshipful rascal, the groom of his close-stool, says, ‘It shall not be thus’, claps the door after him, and who dares enter? A prentice, quoth you? ’Tis but to learn to live, and does that disgrace a man? He that rises hardly stands firmly; but he that rises with ease, alas, falls as easily.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: A pox on you, who taught you this morality?

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: ’Tis ’long of this witty age, Master Francis. But indeed, Mistress Sindefy, all trades complain of inconvenience, and therefore ’tis best to have none. The merchant, he complains and says, ‘Traffic is subject to much uncertainty and loss.’ Let ’em keep their goods on dry land, with a vengeance, and not expose other men’s substances to the mercy of the winds, under protection of a wooden wall, as Master Francis says, and all for greedy desire to enrich themselves with unconscionable gain, two for one, or so; where I, and such other honest men as live by lending money, are content with moderate profit – thirty or forty i’th’hundred, so we may have it with quietness and out of peril of wind and weather, rather than run those dangerous courses of trading, as they do.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Ay, Dad, thou mayst well be called Security, for thou takest the safest course.

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: Faith, the quieter, and the more contented, and, out of doubt, the more godly. For merchants in their courses are never pleased, but ever repining against heaven. One prays for a westerly wind to carry his ship forth; another for an easterly to bring his ship home; and at every shaking of a leaf he falls into an agony to think what danger his ship is in on such a coast, and so forth. The farmer, he is ever at odds with the weather. Sometimes the clouds have been too barren; sometimes the heavens forget themselves, their harvests answer not their hopes; sometimes the season falls out too fruitful, corn will bear no price, and so forth. Th’artificer, he’s all for a stirring world; if his trade be too dull and fall short of his expectation, then falls he out of joint. Where we that trade nothing but money are free from all this. We are pleased with all weathers: let it rain or hold up, be calm or windy, let the season be whatsoever, let trade go how it will, we take all in good part, e’en what please the heavens to send us, so the sun stand not still and the moon keep her usual returns and make up days, months, and years.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: And you have good security?

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: Ay, marry, Frank, that’s the special point.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: And yet, forsooth, we must have trades to live withal, for we cannot stand without legs nor fly without wings, and a number of such scurvy phrases. No, I say still, he that has wit, let him live by his wit; he that has none, let him be a tradesman.

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: Witty Master Francis! ’Tis pity any trade should dull that quick brain of yours. Do but bring Knight Petronel into my parchment toils once, and you shall never need to toil in any trade, o’my credit. You know his wife’s land?

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Even to a foot, sir, I have been often there. A pretty fine seat, good land, all entire within itself.

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: Well wooded?

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Two hundred pounds’ worth of wood ready to fell, and a fine sweet house that stands just in the midst on’t, like a prick in the midst of a circle. Would I were your farmer, for a hundred pound a year!

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: Excellent Master Francis, how I do long to do thee good! How I do hunger and thirst to have the honour to enrich thee! Ay, even to die, that thou mightest inherit my living. Even hunger and thirst! For o’my religion, Master Francis – and so tell Knight Petronel – I do it to do him a pleasure.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Marry, Dad, his horses are now coming up to bear down his lady. Wilt thou lend him thy stable to set ’em in?

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: Faith, Master Francis, I would be loath to lend my stable out of doors. In a greater matter I will pleasure him, but not in this.

p.seg: A pox of your ‘hunger and thirst’! –

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: Now, a frank gale of wind go with him, Master Frank! We have too few such knight adventurers. Who would not sell away competent certainties to purchase, with any danger, excellent uncertainties? Your true knight venturer ever does it. Let his wife seal today; he shall have his money today.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Tomorrow she shall, Dad, before she goes into the country; to work her to which action with the more engines, I purpose presently to prefer my sweet Sin here to the place of her gentlewoman; whom you, for the more credit, shall present as your friend’s daughter, a gentlewoman of the country, new come up with a will for a while to learn fashions, forsooth, and be toward some lady; and she shall buzz pretty devices into her lady’s ear, feeding her humours so serviceably – as the manner of such as she is you know –

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: True, good Master Francis.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: That she shall keep her port open to anything she commends to her.

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: O’my religion, a most fashionable project. As good she spoil the lady as the lady spoil her, for ’tis three to one of one side. Sweet Mistress Sin, how are you bound to Master Francis! I do not doubt to see you shortly wed one of the head men of our city.

sp.speaker: SINDEFY
sp.p: But sweet Frank, when shall my father Security present me?

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: With all festination. I have broken the ice to it already, and will presently to the knight’s house, whither, my good old Dad, let me pray thee with all formality to man her.

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: Command me, Master Francis; I do hunger and thirst to do thee service. – Come, sweet Mistress Sin, take leave of my Winifred, and we will instantly meet frank Master Francis at your lady’s.

sp.speaker: WINIFRED
sp.p: Where is my Cu there? Cu?

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: Ay, Winnie.

sp.speaker: WINIFRED
sp.p: Wilt thou come in, sweet Cu?

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: Ay, Winnie, presently.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: ‘Ay, Winnie’, quod he? That’s all he can do, poor man; he may well cut off her name at Winnie. Oh, ’tis an egregious pandar! What will not an usurous knave be, so he may be rich? Oh, ’tis a notable Jew’s trump! I hope to live to see dog’s meat made of the old usurer’s flesh, dice of his bones and indentures of his skin; and yet his skin is too thick to make parchment, ’twould make good boots for a peterman to catch salmon in. Your only smooth skin to make fine vellum is your puritan’s skin; they be the smoothest and slickest knaves in a country.

div2.stage: Enter SIR PETRONEL in boots with a riding wand [followed by QUICKSILVER].

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: I’ll out of this wicked town as fast as my horse can trot. Here’s now no good action for a man to spend his time in. Taverns grow dead; ordinaries are blown up; plays are at a stand; houses of hospitality at a fall; not a feather waving nor a spur jingling anywhere. I’ll away instantly.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: You’d best take some crowns in your purse, knight, or else your eastward castle will smoke but miserably.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: Oh, Frank! My castle? Alas, all the castles I have are built with air, thou know’st.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: I know it, knight, and therefore wonder whither your lady is going.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: Faith, to seek her fortune, I think. I said I had a castle and land eastward, and eastward she will without contradiction; her coach and the coach of the sun must meet full butt. And the sun being outshined with Her Ladyship’s glory, she fears he goes westward to hang himself.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: And I fear, when her enchanted castle becomes invisible, Her Ladyship will return and follow his example.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: Oh, that she would have the grace, for I shall never be able to pacify her when she sees herself deceived so.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: As easily as can be. Tell her she mistook your directions, and that shortly yourself will down with her to approve it. And then, clothe but her crupper in a new gown and you may drive her any way you list. For these women, sir, are like Essex calves: you must wriggle ’em on by the tail still, or they will never drive orderly.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: But alas, sweet Frank, thou know’st my ability will not furnish her blood with those costly humours.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Cast that cost on me, sir; I have spoken to my old pandar, Security, for money or commodity, and commodity, if you will, I know he will procure you.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: Commodity! Alas, what commodity?

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Why, sir, what say you to figs and raisins?

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: A plague of figs and raisins and all such frail commodities! We shall make nothing of ’em.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Why, then, sir, what say you to forty pound in roasted beef?

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: Out upon’t, I have less stomach to that than to the figs and raisins. I’ll out of town, though I sojourn with a friend of mine, for stay here I must not; my creditors have laid to arrest me, and I have no friend under heaven but my sword to bail me.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: God’s me, knight, put ’em in sufficient sureties rather than let your sword bail you. Let ’em take their choice, either the King’s Bench or the Fleet, or which of the two Counters they like best, for, by the Lord, I like none of ’em.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: Well, Frank, there is no jesting with my earnest necessity; thou know’st if I make not present money to further my voyage begun, all’s lost, and all I have laid out about it.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Why, then, sir, in earnest: if you can get your wise lady to set her hand to the sale of her inheritance, the bloodhound Security will smell out ready money for you instantly.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: There spake an angel! To bring her to which conformity, I must feign myself extremely amorous, and, alleging urgent excuses for my stay behind, part with her as passionately as she would from her foisting hound.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: You have the sow by the right ear, sir. I warrant there was never child longed more to ride a cockhorse or wear his new coat than she longs to ride in her new coach. She would long for everything when she was a maid, and now she will run mad for ’em. I lay my life she will have every year four children; and what charge and change of humour you must endure while she is with child, and how she will tie you to your tackling till she be with child, a dog would not endure. Nay, there is no turnspit dog bound to his wheel more servilely than you shall be to her wheel. For as that dog can never climb the top of his wheel but when the top comes under him, so shall you never climb the top of her contentment but when she is under you.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: ’Slight, how thou terrifiest me!

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Nay, hark you, sir. What nurses, what midwives, what fools, what physicians, what cunning women must be sought for – fearing sometimes she is bewitched, sometimes in a consumption – to tell her tales, to talk bawdy to her, to make her laugh, to give her glisters, to let her blood under the tongue and betwixt the toes; how she will revile and kiss you, spit in your face and lick it off again; how she will vaunt you are her creature, she made you of nothing; how she could have had thousand mark jointures; she could have been made a lady by a Scotch knight and never ha’ married him; she could have had panadas in her bed every morning; how she set you up, and how she will pull you down – you’ll never be able to stand of your legs to endure it.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: Out of my fortune, what a death is my life bound face-to-face to! The best is, a large, time-fitted conscience is bound to nothing. Marriage is but a form in the school of policy, to which scholars sit fastened only with painted chains. Old Security’s young wife is ne’er the further off with me.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Thereby lies a tale, sir. The old usurer will be here instantly with my punk Sindefy, whom you know your lady has promised me to entertain for her gentlewoman, and he – with a purpose to feed on you – invites you most solemnly by me to supper.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: It falls out excellently fitly. I see desire of gain makes jealousy venturous. (Enter GERTRUDE. ) See, Frank, here comes my lady. Lord, how she views thee! She knows thee not, I think, in this bravery.

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: How now? Who be you, I pray?

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: One Master Francis Quicksilver, an’t please Your Ladyship.

p.seg: God’s my dignity! As I am a lady, if he did not make me blush so that mine eyes stood a-water! Would I were unmarried again.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: See, madam, she now comes to attend you.

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: God save my honourable knight and his worshipful lady!

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: You’re very welcome. You must not put on your hat yet.

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: No, madam, till I know Your Ladyship’s further pleasure I will not presume.

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: And is this a gentleman’s daughter new come out of the country?

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: She is, madam, and one that her father hath a special care to bestow in some honourable lady’s service, to put her out of her honest humours, forsooth, for she had a great desire to be a nun, an’t please you.

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: A nun? What nun? A nun substantive or a nun adjective?

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: A nun substantive, madam, I hope, if a nun be a noun. But I mean, lady, a vowed maid of that order.

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: I’ll teach her to be a maid of the order, I warrant you. [To Sindefy] And can you do any work belongs to a lady’s chamber?

sp.speaker: SINDEFY
sp.p: What I cannot do, madam, I would be glad to learn.

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: Well said. Hold up, then; hold up your head, I say. Come hither a little.

sp.speaker: SINDEFY
sp.p: I thank Your Ladyship.

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: And hark you – [To Security] Good man, you may put on your hat now, I do not look on you – I must have you of my faction now, not of my knight’s, maid.

sp.speaker: SINDEFY
sp.p: No, forsooth, madam, of yours.

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: And draw all my servants in my bow, and keep my counsel, and tell me tales, and put me riddles, and read on a book sometimes when I am busy, and laugh at country gentlewomen, and command anything in the house for my retainers, and care not what you spend, for it is all mine; and in any case be still a maid, whatsoever you do, or whatsoever any man can do unto you.

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: I warrant Your Ladyship for that.

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: Very well. You shall ride in my coach with me into the country tomorrow morning. – Come, knight, pray thee let’s make a short supper, and to bed presently.

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: Nay, good madam, this night I have a short supper at home waits on His Worship’s acceptation.

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: By my faith, but he shall not go, sir; I shall swoon an he sup from me.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: Pray thee, forbear. Shall he lose his provision?

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: Ay, by’r Lady, sir, rather than I lose my longing. Come in, I say. As I am a lady, you shall not go!

p.seg: I told him what a bur he had gotten.

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: If you will not sup from your knight, madam, let me entreat Your Ladyship to sup at my house with him.

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: No, by my faith, sir, then we cannot be abed soon enough after supper.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: What a medicine is this! Well, Master Security, you are new married as well as I; I hope you are bound as well. We must honour our young wives, you know.

p.seg: In policy, Dad, till tomorrow she has sealed.

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: I hope in the morning yet your knighthood will breakfast with me?

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: As early as you will, sir.

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: Thank Your good Worship; I do hunger and thirst to do you good, sir.

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: Come, sweet knight, come. I do hunger and thirst to be abed with thee.

div2.stage: Enter PETRONEL, QUICKSILVER, SECURITY, BRAMBLE, and WINIFRED.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: Thanks for our feastlike breakfast, good Master Security. I am sorry, by reason of my instant haste to so long a voyage as Virginia, I am without means by any kind amends to show how affectionately I take your kindness, and to confirm by some worthy ceremony a perpetual league of friendship betwixt us.

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: Excellent knight, let this be a token betwixt us of inviolable friendship. I am new married to this fair gentlewoman, you know, and, by my hope to make her fruitful, though I be something in years, I vow faithfully unto you to make you godfather, though in your absence, to the first child I am blest withal. And henceforth call me gossip, I beseech you, if you please to accept it.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: In the highest degree of gratitude, my most worthy gossip. For confirmation of which friendly title, let me entreat my fair gossip, your wife here, to accept this diamond and keep it as my gift to her first child, wheresoever my fortune in event of my voyage shall bestow me.

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: How now, my coy wedlock, make you strange of so noble a favour? Take it, I charge you, with all affection, and, by way of taking your leave, present boldly your lips to our honourable gossip.

p.seg: How vent’rous he is to him, and how jealous to others!

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: [Kissing Winifred] Long may this kind touch of our lips print in our hearts all the forms of affection! – And now, my good gossip, if the writings be ready to which my wife should seal, let them be brought this morning before she takes coach into the country, and my kindness shall work her to dispatch it.

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: The writings are ready, sir. My learned counsel here, Master Bramble the lawyer, hath perused them, and within this hour I will bring the scrivener with them to your worshipful lady.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: Good Master Bramble, I will here take my leave of you, then. God send you fortunate pleas, sir, and contentious clients!

sp.speaker: BRAMBLE
sp.p: And you foreright winds, sir, and a fortunate voyage!

sp.speaker: MESSENGER
sp.p: Sir Petronel, here are three or four gentlemen desire to speak with you.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: What are they?

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: They are your followers in this voyage, knight, Captain Seagull and his associates. I met them this morning and told them you would be here.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: [To the Messenger] Let them enter, I pray you. [Exit Messenger.] I know they long to be gone, for their stay is dangerous.

sp.speaker: SEAGULL
sp.p: God save my honourable Colonel!

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: Welcome, good Captain Seagull, and worthy gentlemen! If you will meet my friend Frank here, and me, at the Blue Anchor Tavern by Billingsgate this evening, we will there drink to our happy voyage, be merry, and take boat to our ship with all expedition.

sp.speaker: SPENDALL
sp.p: Defer it no longer, I beseech you, sir; but as your voyage is hitherto carried closely and in another knight’s name, so for your own safety and ours let it be continued, our meeting and speedy purpose of departing known to as few as is possible , lest your ship and goods be attached.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Well advised, Captain. Our colonel shall have money this morning to dispatch all our departures. Bring those gentlemen at night to the place appointed, and with our skins full of vintage we’ll take occasion by the vantage, and away.

sp.speaker: SPENDALL
sp.p: We will not fail but be there, sir.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: Good morrow, good Captain, and my worthy associates. [To Winifred] Health and all sovereignty to my beautiful gossip! [To Security] For you, sir, we shall see you presently with the writings.

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: With writings and crowns to my honourable gossip. I do hunger and thirst to do you good, sir! Exeunt.

div2.stage: Enter a COACHMAN in haste, in’s frock, feeding.

sp.speaker: COACHMAN
sp.p: Here’s a stir when citizens ride out of town, indeed, as if all the house were afire! ’Slight, they will not give a man leave to eat ’s breakfast afore he rises.

div2.stage: Enter HAMLET, a footman, in haste.

sp.speaker: HAMLET
sp.p: What, Coachman! My lady’s coach, for shame! Her Ladyship’s ready to come down.

sp.speaker: POTKIN
sp.p: ’Sfoot, Hamlet, are you mad? Whither run you now? You should brush up my old mistress!

sp.speaker: SINDEFY
sp.p: What, Potkin! You must put off your tankard and put on your blue coat and wait upon Mistress Touchstone into the country.

sp.speaker: POTKIN
sp.p: I will, forsooth, presently.

div2.stage: Enter MISTRESS FOND and MISTRESS GAZER.

sp.speaker: FOND
sp.p: Come, sweet Mistress Gazer, let’s watch here and see my Lady Flash take coach.

sp.speaker: GAZER
sp.p: O’my word, here’s a most fine place to stand in. Did you see the new ship launched last day, Mistress Fond?

sp.speaker: FOND
sp.p: Oh, God, and we citizens should lose such a sight!

sp.speaker: GAZER
sp.p: I warrant, here will be double as many people to see her take coach as there were to see it take water.

sp.speaker: FOND
sp.p: Oh, she’s married to a most fine castle i’th’country, they say.

sp.speaker: GAZER
sp.p: But there are no giants in the castle, are there?

sp.speaker: FOND
sp.p: Oh, no, they say her knight killed ’em all, and therefore he was knighted.

sp.speaker: GAZER
sp.p: Would to God Her Ladyship would come away!

div2.stage: Enter GERTRUDE, MISTRESS TOUCHSTONE, SINDEFY, HAMLET, [and] POTKIN.

sp.speaker: FOND
sp.p: She comes, she comes, she comes!

sp.speaker: GAZER [and] FOND
sp.p: Pray heaven bless Your Ladyship!

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: Thank you, good people. My coach, for the love of heaven, my coach! In good truth, I shall swoon else.

sp.speaker: HAMLET
sp.p: Coach, coach, my lady’s coach! Exit.

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: As I am a lady, I think I am with child already, I long for a coach so. May one be with child afore they are married, mother?

sp.speaker: MRS TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: Ay, by’r lady, madam, a little thing does that. I have seen a little prick no bigger than a pin’s head swell bigger and bigger till it has come to an ancome, and e’en so ’tis in these cases.

sp.speaker: HAMLET
sp.p: Your coach is coming, madam.

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: That’s well said. Now, heaven! Methinks I am e’en up to the knees in preferment.

lg.l: [Sing.] ‘But a little higher, but a little higher, but a little higher,
There, there, there lies Cupid’s fire.’

sp.speaker: MRS TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: But must this young man, an’t please you, madam, run by your coach all the way afoot?

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: Ay, by my faith, I warrant him. He gives no other milk, as I have another servant does.

sp.speaker: MRS TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: Alas! ’Tis e’en pity, methinks. For God’s sake, madam, buy him but a hobby-horse; let the poor youth have something betwixt his legs to ease ’em. Alas, we must do as we would be done to.

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: Go to, hold your peace, dame. You talk like an old fool, I tell you.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: Wilt thou be gone, sweet honeysuckle, before I can go with thee?

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: I pray thee, sweet knight, let me; I do so long to dress up thy castle afore thou com’st. But I mar’l how my modest sister occupies herself this morning, that she cannot wait on me to my coach as well as her mother.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Marry, madam, she’s married by this time to prentice Golding. Your father, and someone more, stole to church with ’em in all the haste, that the cold meat left at your wedding might serve to furnish their nuptial table.

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: There’s no base fellow, my father, now, but he’s e’en fit to father such a daughter. He must call me daughter no more now, but ‘madam’, and ‘please you, madam’, and ‘please Your Worship, madam’, indeed. Out upon him! Marry his daughter to a base prentice!

sp.speaker: MRS TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: What should one do? Is there no law for one that marries a woman’s daughter against her will? How shall we punish him, madam?

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: As I am a lady, an’t would snow, we’d so pebble ’em with snowballs as they come from church! But sirrah, Frank Quicksilver –

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Ay, madam.

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: Dost remember since thou and I clapped what-d’ye-call’ts in the garret?

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: I know not what you mean, madam.

lg.l: [Sings.] ‘His head as white as milk,
All flaxen was his hair;
But now he is dead,
And laid in his bed,
And never will come again.’
God be at your labour!

div2.stage: Enter TOUCHSTONE, GOLDING, [and] MILDRED with rosemary.

p.seg: Was there ever such a lady?

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: See, madam, the bride and bridegroom!

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: God’s my precious! God give you joy, Mistress What-lack-you! Now out upon thee, baggage, my sister married in a taffeta hat? Marry, hang you! Westward with a wanion t’ye! Nay, I have done wi’ye, minion, then, i’faith; never look to have my count’nance any more, nor anything I can do for thee. Thou ride in my coach? Or come down to my castle? Fie upon thee! I charge thee in My Ladyship’s name, call me sister no more.

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: An’t please Your Worship, this is not your sister. This is my daughter, and she calls me father, and so does not Your Ladyship, an’t please Your Worship, madam.

sp.speaker: MRS TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: No, nor she must not call thee father by heraldry, because thou mak’st thy prentice thy son as well as she. [To Golding] Ah, thou misproud prentice, dar’st thou presume to marry a lady’s sister?

sp.speaker: GOLDING
sp.p: It pleased my master, forsooth, to embolden me with his favour. And though I confess myself far unworthy so worthy a wife (being in part her servant, as I am your prentice) yet (since I may say it without boasting) I am born a gentleman, and by the trade I have learned of my master (which I trust taints not my blood) able with mine own industry and portion to maintain your daughter, my hope is, heaven will so bless our humble beginning that in the end I shall be no disgrace to the grace with which my master hath bound me his double prentice.

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: ‘Master’ me no more, son, if thou think’st me worthy to be thy father.

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: ‘Son’! Now, good lord, how he shines, an you mark him! He’s a gentleman!

sp.speaker: GOLDING
sp.p: Ay, indeed, madam, a gentleman born.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: Never stand o’your gentry, master bridegroom. If your legs be no better than your arms, you’ll be able to stand upon neither shortly.

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: An’t please Your good Worship, sir, there are two sorts of gentlemen.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: What mean you, sir?

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: Bold to put off my hat to Your Worship –

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: Nay, pray forbear, sir, and then forth with your two sorts of gentlemen.

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: If Your Worship will have it so, I say there are two sorts of gentlemen. There is a gentleman artificial, and a gentleman natural. Now, though Your Worship be a gentleman natural – Work upon that, now!

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Well said, old Touchstone; I am proud to hear thee enter a set speech, i’faith. Forth, I beseech thee.

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: Cry you mercy, sir, Your Worship’s a gentleman I do not know. If you be one of my acquaintance you’re very much disguised, sir.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Go to, old quipper! Forth with thy speech, I say.

sp.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: What, sir, my speeches were ever in vain to Your gracious Worship, and therefore till I speak to you gallantry indeed I will save my breath for my broth anon. – Come, my poor son and daughter, let us hide ourselves in our poor humility and live safe. Ambition consumes itself with the very show. Work upon that now!

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: Let him go, let him go, for God’s sake. Let him make his prentice his son, for God’s sake; give away his daughter, for God’s sake; and when they come a-begging to us, for God’s sake, let’s laugh at their good husbandry, for God’s sake! Farewell, sweet knight; pray thee make haste after.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: What shall I say? I would not have thee go.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER

lg.l: [Sings.] ‘Now, Oh, now, I must depart;
Parting though it absence move’–

sp.p: This ditty, knight, do I see in thy looks in capital letters.

lg.l: [Sings.] ‘What a grief ’tis to depart,
And leave the flower that has my heart!
My sweet lady, and alack for woe,
Why should we part so?’–

sp.p: Tell truth, knight, and shame all dissembling lovers: does not your pain lie on that side?

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: If it do, canst thou tell me how I may cure it?

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Excellent easily: divide yourself in two halves, just by the girdlestead; send one half with your lady, and keep the tother yourself. Or else do as all true lovers do: part with your heart and leave your body behind. I have seen’t done a hundred times. ’Tis as easy a matter for a lover to part without a heart from his sweetheart, and he ne’er the worse, as for a mouse to get from a trap and leave his tail behind him. See, here comes the writings.

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: Good morrow to My worshipful Lady! I present Your Ladyship with this writing, to which if you please to set your hand, with your knight’s, a velvet gown shall attend your journey, o’my credit.

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: What writing is it, knight?

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: The sale, sweetheart, of the poor tenement I told thee of, only to make a little money to send thee down furniture for my castle, to which my hand shall lead thee.

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: Very well. Now give me your pen, I pray.

p.seg: It goes down without chewing, i’faith.

sp.speaker: SCRIVENER
sp.p: Your Worships deliver this as your deed?

sp.speaker: BOTH [GERTRUDE and PETRONEL]
sp.p: We do.

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: So now, knight, farewell till I see thee.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: All farewell to my sweetheart!

sp.speaker: MRS TOUCHSTONE
sp.p: God b’ye, son knight.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: Farewell, my good mother.

sp.speaker: GERTRUDE
sp.p: Farewell, Frank. I would fain take thee down if I could.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: I thank Your good Ladyship. Farewell, Mistress Sindefy.

div2.stage: Exeunt [all except Petronel, Quicksilver, and Security].

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: Oh, tedious voyage, whereof there is no end! What will they think of me?

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Think what they list. They longed for a vagary into the country, and now they are fitted. So a woman marry to ride in a coach, she cares not if she ride to her ruin. ’Tis the great end of many of their marriages. This is not the first time a lady has rid a false journey in her coach, I hope.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: Nay, ’tis no matter; I care little what they think. He that weighs men’s thoughts has his hands full of nothing. A man in the course of this world should be like a surgeon’s instrument: work in the wounds of others and feel nothing himself. The sharper and subtler, the better.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: As it falls out now, knight, you shall not need to devise excuses or endure her outcries when she returns; we shall now be gone before where they cannot reach us.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: [To Security] Well, my kind compeer, you have now th’assurance we both can make you. Let me now entreat you the money we agreed on may be brought to the Blue Anchor near to Billingsgate by six o’clock, where I and my chief friends, bound for this voyage, will with feasts attend you.

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: The money, my most honourable compeer, shall without fail observe your appointed hour.

lg.l: Thanks, my dear gossip. I must now impart
To your approvèd love a loving secret,
As one on whom my life doth more rely
In friendly trust than any man alive.
Nor shall you be the chosen secretary
Of my affections for affection only;
For I protest (if God bless my return)
To make you partner in my action’s gain
As deeply as if you had ventured with me
Half my expenses. Know then, honest gossip,
I have enjoyed with such divine contentment
A gentlewoman’s bed, whom you well know,
That I shall ne’er enjoy this tedious voyage,
Nor live the least part of the time it asketh,
Without her presence, so I thirst and hunger
To taste the dear feast of her company.
And if the hunger and the thirst you vow
As my sworn gossip to my wishèd good
Be – as I know it is – unfeigned and firm,
Do me an easy favour in your power.
Be sure, brave gossip, all that I can do,
To my best nerve, is wholly at your service.
Who is the woman, first, that is your friend?
The woman is your learnèd counsel’s wife,
The lawyer, Master Bramble; whom would you
Bring out this even, in honest neighbourhood,
To take his leave with you of me, your gossip,
I, in the meantime, will send this my friend
Home to his house, to bring his wife disguised
Before his face into our company.
For love hath made her look for such a wile
To free her from his tyrannous jealousy,
And I would take this course before another,
In stealing her away to make us sport
And gull his circumspection the more grossly.
And I am sure that no man like yourself
Hath credit with him to entice his jealousy
To so long stay abroad as may give time
To her enlargement in such safe disguise.
A pretty, pithy, and most pleasant project!
Who would not strain a point of neighbourhood
For such a point-device, that, as the ship
Of famous Draco went about the world,
Will wind about the lawyer, compassing
The world himself? He hath it in his arms,
And that’s enough for him without his wife.
A lawyer is ambitious, and his head
Cannot be praised nor raised too high
With any fork of highest knavery.
I’ll go fetch him straight. Exit Security.
So, so. Now, Frank, go thou home to his house,
’Stead of his lawyer’s, and bring his wife hither,
Who, just like to the lawyer’s wife, is prisoned
With his stern, usurous jealousy, which could never
Be overreached thus but with overreaching.
And, Master Francis, watch you th’instant time
To enter with his exit. ’Twill be rare:
Two fine horned beasts, a camel and a lawyer!
How the old villain joys in villainy!
And hark you, gossip, when you have her here,
Have your boat ready; ship her to your ship
With utmost haste, lest Master Bramble stay you.
To o’erreach that head that outreacheth all heads,
’Tis a trick rampant, ’tis a very quiblin!
I hope this harvest to pitch cart with lawyers,
Their heads will be so forked. This sly touch
Will get apes to invent a number such.
Was ever rascal honied so with poison?
He that delights in slavish avarice
Is apt to joy in every sort of vice.
Well, I’ll go fetch his wife, whilst he the lawyer.
But stay, Frank, let’s think how we may disguise her
Upon this sudden.
God’s me, there’s the mischief!
But hark you, here’s an excellent device,
’Fore God, a rare one: I will carry her
A sailor’s gown and cap and cover her,
And a player’s beard.
And what upon her head?
I tell you, a sailor’s cap. ’Slight, God forgive me,
What kind of figent memory have you?
Nay, then, what kind of figent wit hast thou?
A sailor’s cap? How shall she put it off
When thou present’st her to our company?
Tush, man, for that, make her a saucy sailor.
Tush, tush, ’tis no fit sauce for such sweet mutton;
I know not what t’advise.

div2.stage: Enter SECURITY with his wife’s gown.

lg.l: Knight, knight, a rare device!
What stratagem have you now?
The best that ever. You talked of disguising?
Ay, marry, gossip, that’s our present care.
Cast care away, then. Here’s the best device
For plain Security – for I am no better –
I think that ever lived. Here’s my wife’s gown,
Which you may put upon the lawyer’s wife,
And which I brought you, sir, for two great reasons:
One is, that Master Bramble may take hold
Of some suspicion that it is my wife,
And gird me so, perhaps, with his law wit;
The other (which is policy indeed)
Is that my wife may now be tied at home,
Having no more but her old gown abroad,
And not show me a quirk while I firk others.
Is not this rare?
The best that ever was!
Am I not born to furnish gentlemen?
O my dear gossip!
Well, hold, Master Francis;
Watch when the lawyer’s out, and put it in.
And now I will go fetch him.
O my Dad!

l.seg: He goes as ’twere the devil to fetch the lawyer;
And devil shall he be, if horns will make him.

lg.l: [To Security] Why, how now, gossip, why stay you there musing?
A toy, a toy runs in my head, i’faith.

l.seg: A pox of that head! Is there more toys yet?

lg.l: What is it, pray thee, gossip?
Why, sir, what if you
Should slip away now with my wife’s best gown,
I having no security for it?
For that, I hope, Dad, you will take our words.

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: Ay, by th’Mass, your word! That’s a proper staff

lg.l: For wise Security to lean upon!
But ’tis no matter. Once I’ll trust my name
On your cracked credits; let it take no shame.
Fetch the wench, Frank.
I’ll wait upon you, sir –
And fetch you over, you were ne’er so fetched.
[To Petronel] Go, to the tavern, knight; your followers
Dare not be drunk, I think, before their captain.
Would I might lead them to no hotter service,
Till our Virginian gold were in our purses!

div2.stage: Enter SEAGULL, SPENDALL, and SCAPETHRIFT in the tavern with a DRAWER.

sp.speaker: SEAGULL
sp.p: Come, Drawer, pierce your neatest hogsheads, and let’s have cheer not fit for your Billingsgate tavern but for our Virginian colonel; he will be here instantly.

sp.speaker: DRAWER
sp.p: You shall have all things fit, sir. Please you have any more wine?

sp.speaker: SPENDALL
sp.p: More wine, slave? Whether we drink it or no, spill it, and draw more.

sp.speaker: SCAPETHRIFT
sp.p: Fill all the pots in your house with all sorts of liquor, and let ’em wait on us here like soldiers in their pewter coats. And though we do not employ them now, yet we will maintain ’em till we do.

sp.speaker: DRAWER
sp.p: Said like an honourable captain. You shall have all you can command, sir.

sp.speaker: SEAGULL
sp.p: Come, boys, Virginia longs till we share the rest of her maidenhead.

sp.speaker: SPENDALL
sp.p: Why, is she inhabited already with any English?

sp.speaker: SEAGULL
sp.p: A whole country of English is there, man, bred of those that were left there in ’79. They have married with the Indians and make ’em bring forth as beautiful faces as any we have in England, and therefore the Indians are so in love with ’em that all the treasure they have, they lay at their feet.

sp.speaker: SCAPETHRIFT
sp.p: But is there such treasure there, Captain, as I have heard?

sp.speaker: SEAGULL
sp.p: I tell thee, gold is more plentiful there than copper is with us, and for as much red copper as I can bring, I’ll have thrice the weight in gold. Why, man, all their dripping pans and their chamber pots are pure gold; and all the chains with which they chain up their streets are massy gold; all the prisoners they take are fettered in gold. And for rubies and diamonds, they go forth on holidays and gather ’em by the seashore to hang on their children’s coats and stick in their caps, as commonly as our children wear saffron-gilt brooches and groats with holes in ’em.

sp.speaker: SCAPETHRIFT
sp.p: And is it a pleasant country withal?

sp.speaker: SEAGULL
sp.p: As ever the sun shined on; temperate and full of all sorts of excellent viands. Wild boar is as common there as our tamest bacon is here, venison as mutton. And then you shall live freely there, without sergeants, or courtiers, or lawyers, or intelligencers; only a few industrious Scots, perhaps, who indeed are dispersed over the face of the whole earth. But as for them, there are no greater friends to Englishmen and England, when they are out on’t, in the world than they are. And for my part, I would a hundred thousand of ’em were there, for we are all one countrymen now, ye know, and we should find ten times more comfort of them there than we do here. Then for your means to advancement there, it is simple and not preposterously mixed: you may be an alderman there and never be scavenger; you may be a nobleman and never be a slave. You may come to preferment enough and never be a pander; to riches and fortune enough and have never the more villainy nor the less wit.

sp.speaker: SPENDALL
sp.p: God’s me! And how far is it thither?

sp.speaker: SEAGULL
sp.p: Some six weeks’ sail, no more, with any indifferent good wind. And if I get to any part of the coast of Africa, I’ll sail thither with any wind. Or when I come to Cape Finisterre, there’s a foreright wind continually wafts us till we come at Virginia. See, our colonel’s come.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: Well met, good Captain Seagull, and my noble gentlemen! Now the sweet hour of our freedom is at hand. Come, Drawer. Fill us some carouses, and prepare us for the mirth that will be occasioned presently. [Drawer pours wine.] [Exit Drawer.] Here will be a pretty wench, gentlemen, that will bear us company all our voyage.

sp.speaker: SEAGULL
sp.p: Whatsoever she be, here’s to her health, noble Colonel, both with cap and knee.

div2.stage: [He removes his cap, kneels, and drinks.]

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: Thanks, kind Captain Seagull. She’s one I love dearly, and must not be known till we be free from all that know us. And so, gentlemen, here’s to her health!

sp.speaker: BOTH [SPENDALL and SCAPETHRIFT]
sp.p: Let it come, worthy Colonel! We do hunger and thirst for it.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: Afore heaven, you have hit the phrase of one that her presence will touch from the foot to the forehead, if ye knew it.

sp.speaker: SPENDALL
sp.p: Why, then, we will join his forehead with her health, sir. And Captain Scapethrift, here’s to ’em both.

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: See, see, Master Bramble! ’Fore heaven, their voyage cannot but prosper; they are o’their knees for success to it.

sp.speaker: BRAMBLE
sp.p: And they pray to God Bacchus.

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: God save my brave colonel, with all his tall captains and corporals! See, sir, my worshipful learned counsel, Master Bramble, is come to take his leave of you.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: [As he and the sailors rise.] Worshipful Master Bramble, how far do you draw us into the sweet briar of your kindness? Come, Captain Seagull, another health to this rare Bramble, that hath never a prick about him.

sp.speaker: SEAGULL
sp.p: I pledge his most smooth disposition, sir. Come, Master Security, bend your supporters and pledge this notorious health here.

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: Bend you yours likewise, Master Bramble, for it is you shall pledge me.

sp.speaker: SEAGULL
sp.p: Not so, Master Security; he must not pledge his own health.

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: No, Master Captain?

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: Why, then, here’s one is fitly come to do him that honour.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: [To Petronel] Here’s the gentlewoman your cousin, sir, whom with much entreaty I have brought to take her leave of you in a tavern; ashamed whereof, you must pardon her if she put not off her mask.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: Pardon me, sweet cousin. My kind desire to see you before I went made me so importunate to entreat your presence here.

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: How now, Master Francis? Have you honoured this presence with a fair gentlewoman?

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Pray, sir, take you no notice of her, for she will not be known to you.

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: But my learned counsel, Master Bramble here, I hope may know her.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: No more than you, sir, at this time; his learning must pardon her.

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: Well, God pardon her for my part, and I do, I’ll be sworn. And so, Master Francis, here’s to all that are going eastward tonight, towards Cuckold’s Haven; and so to the health of Master Bramble.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: [Kneeling] I pledge it, sir. Hath it gone round, captains?

sp.speaker: SEAGULL
sp.p: It has, sweet Frank, and the round closes with thee.

sp.speaker: QUICKSILVER
sp.p: Well, sir, here’s to all eastward and toward cuckolds, and so to famous Cuckold’s Haven so fatally remembered.

sp.speaker: PETRONEL
sp.p: [To Winifred] Nay, pray thee, coz, weep not. – Gossip Security?

sp.speaker: SECURITY
sp.p: Ay, my brave gossip?

p.seg: Our friend, Mistress Bramble here, is so dissolved in tears that she drowns the whole mirth of our meeting. Sweet gossip, take her aside and comfort her.
